chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
A bad character/temper ruins deeds, just as vinegar ruins honey.
ai.seo_question: How does bad character affect the validity of good deeds in Islam?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) employs the vivid analogy of vinegar spoiling honey to illustrate how *khuluq sayy* (bad character) corrupts the spiritual value of good deeds. This teaching, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and moral refinement as essential complements to ritual worship, ensuring that actions are not merely performed but are spiritually pure and accepted.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-96 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “
A bad temper will ruin your deeds as vinegar will ruin the sweetness of honey.”
